questions.question: Although cells are often drawn flat on a page in textbooks, what is their actual shape in reality?
options: They are completely flat 2D surfaces
They have a three-dimensional shape
They are always perfect cubes
They are thin 1D threads

questions.question: Which of the following lists only structures that are commonly found in animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm, cell wall, nucleus, chloroplasts
Cytoplasm, cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria
Cell membrane, vacuole, cell wall, chloroplasts
Nucleus, cell wall, mitochondria, vacuole

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a unicellular organism?
options: It does not contain any genetic material
It is made of a single living cell
It is only found in non-living environments
It is composed of millions of identical cells

questions.question: In a multicellular organism, how are the cells organized to carry out life?
options: The organism is made of more than one cell, and different cells take on different jobs
Every single cell performs every function independently and they do not cooperate
All cells must have the exact same shape and size to work together
There is only one cell that does all the work while others remain inactive

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, what is formed when similar cells join together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ system
A tissue
A unicellular organism
A chloroplast

questions.question: How is an organ defined in multicellular organisms?
options: A single cell that has grown extremely large
A group of tissues working together to do a specific job
A collection of organ systems working independently
The outer protective layer of a plant cell

questions.question: What are the fundamental living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Tissues
Cells
Organs

questions.question: Why do we typically need a microscope to observe individual cells?
options: Cells are usually too small to see with the unaided eye
Cells only exist when light shines on them
Cells are completely transparent to human eyes
Cells move too fast to be seen without a lens

questions.question: Which structures are found in plant cells but are NOT present in animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm and nucleus
Cell membrane and mitochondria
Cell wall, vacuole, and sometimes chloroplasts
Nucleus and cell wall

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a stain to a cell sample on a microscope slide?
options: To kill any bacteria so the cells stop moving
To make it easier to see some parts of the cells
To glue the coverslip permanently to the slide
To increase the magnification power of the lens

questions.question: How should observations of cells made under a light microscope be recorded in a science notebook?
options: Using a highly detailed 3D oil painting
As a scientific line drawing
By writing a fictional story about the cells
With a simple list of chemical formulas

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of specialised cells found in animals and plants?
options: Red blood cells in animals and root hair cells in plants
Nerve cells in animals and muscle cells in plants
Chloroplasts in animals and mitochondria in plants
Cytoplasm in animals and vacuoles in plants

questions.question: Which group contains only essential life processes that happen in all living organisms?
options: Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition
Photosynthesis, circulation, thinking, talking, sleeping, hearing, breathing
Melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing, dissolving, burning, decaying
Walking, crying, playing, reading, writing, calculating, sleeping

questions.question: According to the principles of life processes, how are all living organisms made?
options: They spontaneously appear from non-living dirt and water
They are made from other living organisms when they reproduce
They are manufactured in factories from raw chemical elements
They grow directly from minerals deep inside rocks

questions.question: When is movement considered a sign of life in an organism?
options: When the wind blows the organism from one place to another
When the organism moves itself to achieve something
When gravity pulls the organism downward
When water currents wash the organism away
